definitions.s0: N-r0 upper bound at the first ordinary-elimination state after any root unit propagation

transition_lemma.statement: If a unit-free ordinary state has state_units<=s and T(s)<=N^2, every live pivot is raw-cap safe; after exact ordinary elimination and any unit propagation, the next residual has state_units<=T(s) and at least one fewer live variable.

range_proof.N_le_15: Since r0>=2 in the nontrivial ordinary case, s0<=N-2<=13 and T(s)=s throughout; raw-cap rescue is impossible.
range_proof.conclusion: For every allowed root-variable count and every ordinary step needed to exhaust that budget, the sufficient envelope stays strictly below N^2 through N=19.

theorem.name: NO_RAW_CAP_RESCUE_REQUIRED_THROUGH_N19
theorem.statement: For every legitimate root with frozen input size N<=19, the current frozen solver cannot require v2/v3 because ordinary exact elimination ran out of N^2 raw-cap availability. Earlier exact termination remains allowed.

N20_boundary.statement: The same sufficient recurrence is no longer universal at N=20; for r0=4 it eventually permits an envelope >400. This is certificate failure only, not evidence of an actual N20 solver failure or extension requirement.
